definition.0.title: Purpose
definition.0.placeholder: Describe your purpose approach, boundaries, and verification.
definition.0.example: Resolve support enquiries using approved knowledge; escalate unresolved cases.

definition.1.title: Boundaries
definition.1.placeholder: Describe your boundaries approach, boundaries, and verification.
definition.1.example: Never issue refunds, alter accounts, or disclose another customer’s records.

definition.2.title: Users
definition.2.placeholder: Describe your users approach, boundaries, and verification.
definition.2.example: Authenticated customers and support staff invoke the agent through the support application.

definition.3.title: Inputs & outputs
definition.3.placeholder: Describe your inputs & outputs approach, boundaries, and verification.
definition.3.example: Accept a tenant-scoped enquiry; return an answer, citations, and escalation outcome.

definition.4.title: Model strategy
definition.4.placeholder: Describe your model strategy approach, boundaries, and verification.
definition.4.example: Use an approved primary model; fail over only to providers with equivalent data controls.

definition.5.title: Skills
definition.5.placeholder: Describe your skills approach, boundaries, and verification.
definition.5.example: Expose knowledge lookup, case summarization, and escalation preparation.

definition.6.title: Autonomy
definition.6.placeholder: Describe your autonomy approach, boundaries, and verification.
definition.6.example: Operate at L2: prepare actions; a human authorizes execution.

definition.7.title: Failure behavior
definition.7.placeholder: Describe your failure behavior approach, boundaries, and verification.
definition.7.example: Retry transient reads within a bounded budget; otherwise explain failure and escalate.

identity.0.title: Agent identity
identity.0.placeholder: Describe your agent identity approach, boundaries, and verification.
identity.0.example: Each deployed agent uses a distinct service identity scoped to its environment.

identity.1.title: Invoker identity
identity.1.placeholder: Describe your invoker identity approach, boundaries, and verification.
identity.1.example: Propagate verified caller and tenant IDs; never trust identity supplied in prompt text.

identity.2.title: Invocation policy
identity.2.placeholder: Describe your invocation policy approach, boundaries, and verification.
identity.2.example: Only authenticated support roles may invoke the private gateway endpoint.

identity.3.title: Delegation
identity.3.placeholder: Describe your delegation approach, boundaries, and verification.
identity.3.example: Allowlisted downstream agents receive restricted authority and verified caller context.

identity.4.title: Tool authorization
identity.4.placeholder: Describe your tool authorization approach, boundaries, and verification.
identity.4.example: Grant read-only knowledge access and case-draft creation; deny other operations.

identity.5.title: Resource authorization
identity.5.placeholder: Describe your resource authorization approach, boundaries, and verification.
identity.5.example: Enforce tenant filters at the resource boundary, not only in model instructions.

identity.6.title: Credential handling
identity.6.placeholder: Describe your credential handling approach, boundaries, and verification.
identity.6.example: Inject short-lived credentials from a secret manager; never place them in prompts or logs.

identity.7.title: Audit attribution
identity.7.placeholder: Describe your audit attribution approach, boundaries, and verification.
identity.7.example: Audit records distinguish requesting user, executing agent, approval actor, and tool identity.

tools.0.title: Tool allowlist
tools.0.placeholder: Describe your tool allowlist approach, boundaries, and verification.
tools.0.example: Expose only versioned tools approved for this agent; enforce authorization at execution.

tools.1.title: Discovery
tools.1.placeholder: Describe your discovery approach, boundaries, and verification.
tools.1.example: Resolve approved tool versions from a registry at startup; do not discover arbitrary servers.

tools.2.title: Input validation
tools.2.placeholder: Describe your input validation approach, boundaries, and verification.
tools.2.example: Validate arguments against schemas and reject out-of-scope tenant or resource IDs.

tools.3.title: Side effects
tools.3.placeholder: Describe your side effects approach, boundaries, and verification.
tools.3.example: Classify lookup as NONE and draft creation as REVERSIBLE; external sends require review.

tools.4.title: Approval boundary
tools.4.placeholder: Describe your approval boundary approach, boundaries, and verification.
tools.4.example: Require explicit approval for outbound messages and account changes; bind approval to exact arguments.

tools.5.title: Failure & retry
tools.5.placeholder: Describe your failure & retry approach, boundaries, and verification.
tools.5.example: Retry safe reads; use idempotency keys for writes and reconcile uncertain outcomes.

memory.0.title: Memory Scope
memory.0.placeholder: Describe your memory scope approach, boundaries, and verification.
memory.0.example: Persist confirmed preferences and case summaries; do not retain credentials or raw sensitive conversations.

memory.1.title: Memory Types
memory.1.placeholder: Describe your memory types approach, boundaries, and verification.
memory.1.example: Case history is episodic, verified preferences semantic, approved workflows procedural.

memory.2.title: Retrieval
memory.2.placeholder: Describe your retrieval approach, boundaries, and verification.
memory.2.example: Retrieve tenant-scoped relevant memories before answering; cap injected context and preserve provenance.

memory.3.title: Write & Consolidation
memory.3.placeholder: Describe your write & consolidation approach, boundaries, and verification.
memory.3.example: Write only verified facts after a run; merge duplicates and flag conflicting sources for review.

memory.4.title: Staleness
memory.4.placeholder: Describe your staleness approach, boundaries, and verification.
memory.4.example: Expire case summaries according to retention policy; invalidate preferences when the source changes.

memory.5.title: Context Budget
memory.5.placeholder: Describe your context budget approach, boundaries, and verification.
memory.5.example: Reserve separate token budgets for instructions, memory, tool results, and recent conversation.

memory.6.title: Governance
memory.6.placeholder: Describe your governance approach, boundaries, and verification.
memory.6.example: Apply tenant-scoped read/write permissions, deletion workflows, retention rules, and memory audit events.

safety.0.title: Autonomy level
safety.0.placeholder: Describe your autonomy level approach, boundaries, and verification.
safety.0.example: Allow L2 preparation only; external execution is denied without human authorization.

safety.1.title: Prompt injection
safety.1.placeholder: Describe your prompt injection approach, boundaries, and verification.
safety.1.example: Treat retrieved pages and tool output as untrusted data; they cannot grant tool authority.

safety.2.title: Data handling
safety.2.placeholder: Describe your data handling approach, boundaries, and verification.
safety.2.example: Classify sensitive fields, minimize model exposure, and redact outputs before delivery.

safety.3.title: Policy enforcement
safety.3.placeholder: Describe your policy enforcement approach, boundaries, and verification.
safety.3.example: Enforce deterministic policy checks before tool execution and before releasing sensitive outputs.

safety.4.title: Human approval
safety.4.placeholder: Describe your human approval approach, boundaries, and verification.
safety.4.example: Require approval for external actions, ambiguous identity, or high-risk data access.

safety.5.title: Verification
safety.5.placeholder: Describe your verification approach, boundaries, and verification.
safety.5.example: Validate target, authority, and expected effect before execution; reconcile the returned receipt afterward.

safety.6.title: Emergency controls
safety.6.placeholder: Describe your emergency controls approach, boundaries, and verification.
safety.6.example: Operators can disable the agent or individual tools immediately and revoke active credentials.

evaluation.0.title: Success definition
evaluation.0.placeholder: Describe your success definition approach, boundaries, and verification.
evaluation.0.example: A successful run resolves the enquiry with supported evidence or correctly escalates.

evaluation.1.title: Golden dataset
evaluation.1.placeholder: Describe your golden dataset approach, boundaries, and verification.
evaluation.1.example: Maintain representative approved enquiries, edge cases, and expected answers with versioned labels.

evaluation.2.title: Tool correctness
evaluation.2.placeholder: Describe your tool correctness approach, boundaries, and verification.
evaluation.2.example: Check selected tool, validated arguments, call sequence, and resulting resource state against expected behavior.

evaluation.3.title: Policy compliance
evaluation.3.placeholder: Describe your policy compliance approach, boundaries, and verification.
evaluation.3.example: Test denied tenants, unauthorized tools, missing approvals, and sensitive-output restrictions.

evaluation.4.title: Regression strategy
evaluation.4.placeholder: Describe your regression strategy approach, boundaries, and verification.
evaluation.4.example: Run golden and adversarial suites on every prompt, model, tool, memory, or policy change.

evaluation.5.title: Production evaluation
evaluation.5.placeholder: Describe your production evaluation approach, boundaries, and verification.
evaluation.5.example: Sample redacted live runs for quality review; restrict reviewer access and retain only necessary evidence.

evaluation.6.title: Release threshold
evaluation.6.placeholder: Describe your release threshold approach, boundaries, and verification.
evaluation.6.example: Illustrative thresholds: task success at least 95%, critical policy violations zero; owners approve actual targets.

delegation.0.title: Delegation policy
delegation.0.placeholder: Describe your delegation policy approach, boundaries, and verification.
delegation.0.example: The support agent may call only the approved knowledge specialist; neither may delegate account changes.

delegation.1.title: Maximum depth
delegation.1.placeholder: Describe your maximum depth approach, boundaries, and verification.
delegation.1.example: Limit delegation to two hops and reject calls exceeding the shared run budget.

delegation.2.title: Identity propagation
delegation.2.placeholder: Describe your identity propagation approach, boundaries, and verification.
delegation.2.example: Use the callee’s scoped identity while carrying verified caller identity for authorization and audit.

delegation.3.title: Context propagation
delegation.3.placeholder: Describe your context propagation approach, boundaries, and verification.
delegation.3.example: Share the enquiry and necessary tenant-scoped facts; exclude credentials and unrelated conversation.

delegation.4.title: Loop prevention
delegation.4.placeholder: Describe your loop prevention approach, boundaries, and verification.
delegation.4.example: Track visited agent IDs and reject cycles; apply a shared hop limit and deadline.

delegation.5.title: Final ownership
delegation.5.placeholder: Describe your final ownership approach, boundaries, and verification.
delegation.5.example: The calling agent owns the final response and communicates downstream failure without inventing results.

runtime.0.title: Environments
runtime.0.placeholder: Describe your environments approach, boundaries, and verification.
runtime.0.example: Use separate development, staging, and production identities, secrets, resources, and deployment approvals.

runtime.1.title: Runtime isolation
runtime.1.placeholder: Describe your runtime isolation approach, boundaries, and verification.
runtime.1.example: Run agents in isolated containers; enforce tenant boundaries in storage and tool authorization.

runtime.2.title: Network
runtime.2.placeholder: Describe your network approach, boundaries, and verification.
runtime.2.example: Permit gateway ingress and allowlisted outbound endpoints; deny arbitrary internet connections.

runtime.3.title: Scaling & concurrency
runtime.3.placeholder: Describe your scaling & concurrency approach, boundaries, and verification.
runtime.3.example: Scale stateless workers within quotas; enforce per-tenant concurrency and queue limits.

runtime.4.title: Sessions
runtime.4.placeholder: Describe your sessions approach, boundaries, and verification.
runtime.4.example: Store encrypted tenant-scoped sessions with expiry; do not rely on worker-local state.

runtime.5.title: Timeouts & retries
runtime.5.placeholder: Describe your timeouts & retries approach, boundaries, and verification.
runtime.5.example: Use a total run deadline with bounded model/tool attempts; do not blindly retry side effects.

runtime.6.title: Deployment
runtime.6.placeholder: Describe your deployment approach, boundaries, and verification.
runtime.6.example: Promote immutable versions through staging and canary rollout; retain a tested rollback version.

runtime.7.title: Availability
runtime.7.placeholder: Describe your availability approach, boundaries, and verification.
runtime.7.example: Define a service availability target and recovery objectives; test dependency failure and restore procedures.

registry.0.title: Canonical ID
registry.0.placeholder: Describe your canonical id approach, boundaries, and verification.
registry.0.example: Assign an immutable agent ID; distinguish versions and environment deployments separately.

registry.1.title: Registry metadata
registry.1.placeholder: Describe your registry metadata approach, boundaries, and verification.
registry.1.example: Require owner, version, runtime, model policy, tool allowlist, classification, and autonomy before approval.

registry.2.title: Lifecycle
registry.2.placeholder: Describe your lifecycle approach, boundaries, and verification.
registry.2.example: Require evaluation and named approval before production; retirement revokes invocation and execution.

registry.3.title: Versioning
registry.3.placeholder: Describe your versioning approach, boundaries, and verification.
registry.3.example: Version changes to prompts, policies, models, and tools; published definitions remain immutable.

registry.4.title: Discovery
registry.4.placeholder: Describe your registry discovery approach, boundaries, and verification.
registry.4.example: Expose approved capabilities to authorized callers without publishing secrets or internal resource details.

registry.5.title: Retirement
registry.5.placeholder: Describe your retirement approach, boundaries, and verification.
registry.5.example: Stop new runs, drain active work, revoke credentials, and apply memory and audit retention policy.

observability.0.title: Trace model
observability.0.placeholder: Describe the root trace, child spans, ID propagation, captured fields, and redaction.
observability.0.example: The gateway starts a root trace; the agent, model calls, tool calls, and delegated runs create child spans. Propagate trace_id across services; record duration, outcome, retries, token usage, and model/tool IDs. Exclude secrets and sensitive content.

observability.1.title: Correlation
observability.1.placeholder: Describe your correlation approach, boundaries, and verification.
observability.1.example: Carry agent_run_id, agent_id, agent_version, session_id, trace_id, caller_id, tool_id, and model_id in scoped telemetry.

observability.2.title: Sensitive telemetry
observability.2.placeholder: Describe your sensitive telemetry approach, boundaries, and verification.
observability.2.example: Never log credentials or raw sensitive prompts; redact identifiers and restrict access to approved metadata.

observability.3.title: Metrics
observability.3.placeholder: Describe your metrics approach, boundaries, and verification.
observability.3.example: Measure successful outcomes, latency, token usage, cost, tool errors, policy denials, and escalation rate.

observability.4.title: Alerts
observability.4.placeholder: Describe your alerts approach, boundaries, and verification.
observability.4.example: Page on sustained service failure or suspected isolation breach; route routine quality deviations to review.

observability.5.title: Audit retention
observability.5.placeholder: Describe your audit retention approach, boundaries, and verification.
observability.5.example: Retain approval and policy audit events under the agreed retention policy with tamper-evident storage.

security.0.title: Trust boundaries
security.0.placeholder: Describe your trust boundaries approach, boundaries, and verification.
security.0.example: Document gateway, model provider, memory store, tool server, and tenant boundaries with allowed data flows.

security.1.title: Identity threats
security.1.placeholder: Describe your identity threats approach, boundaries, and verification.
security.1.example: Verify caller identities and resource scope; reject spoofed delegation and privilege escalation attempts.

security.2.title: Prompt threats
security.2.placeholder: Describe your prompt threats approach, boundaries, and verification.
security.2.example: Separate untrusted content from instructions; validate authority independently before every tool call.

security.3.title: Memory threats
security.3.placeholder: Describe your memory threats approach, boundaries, and verification.
security.3.example: Validate memory provenance and tenant scope; detect poisoning and delete stale sensitive records.

security.4.title: Tool threats
security.4.placeholder: Describe your tool threats approach, boundaries, and verification.
security.4.example: Use approved tool servers, scoped credentials, strict argument validation, and restricted network access.

security.5.title: Data exfiltration
security.5.placeholder: Describe your data exfiltration approach, boundaries, and verification.
security.5.example: Allowlist outbound destinations; minimize provider data exposure and deny unauthorized export tools.

security.6.title: Supply chain
security.6.placeholder: Describe your supply chain approach, boundaries, and verification.
security.6.example: Pin reviewed dependencies and tool definitions; record provenance and revoke compromised versions.

readiness.0.title: Architecture review
readiness.0.placeholder: Describe your architecture review approach, boundaries, and verification.
readiness.0.example: A named reviewer verifies the architecture, unresolved decisions, and supporting evidence before approval.

readiness.1.title: Security review
readiness.1.placeholder: Describe your security review approach, boundaries, and verification.
readiness.1.example: Security owners review the threat model and document remediation or accepted residual risk.

readiness.2.title: Evaluation gate
readiness.2.placeholder: Describe your evaluation gate approach, boundaries, and verification.
readiness.2.example: Attach versioned offline and regression results showing the agreed release thresholds are met.

readiness.3.title: Policy gate
readiness.3.placeholder: Describe your policy gate approach, boundaries, and verification.
readiness.3.example: Verify access controls, approval gates, and runtime restrictions against deployed configuration.

readiness.4.title: Observability gate
readiness.4.placeholder: Describe your observability gate approach, boundaries, and verification.
readiness.4.example: Demonstrate end-to-end tracing, actionable alerts, and an auditable investigation workflow.

readiness.5.title: Operational gate
readiness.5.placeholder: Describe your operational gate approach, boundaries, and verification.
readiness.5.example: Assign on-call ownership and test runbooks, rollback, and emergency disable procedures.

readiness.6.title: Data governance
readiness.6.placeholder: Describe your data governance approach, boundaries, and verification.
readiness.6.example: Verify retention, deletion, redaction, and authorized export behavior with evidence.

readiness.7.title: Launch approval
readiness.7.placeholder: Describe your launch approval approach, boundaries, and verification.
readiness.7.example: The accountable owner records explicit launch approval for the version after all required reviews.
